stories.title: 'Please take the job': Trump asks UFC chief Dana White to be White House press secretary
summary: White ​and ⁠UFC’s parent company, TKO Group Holdings, did not immediately return requests for comment.
Zacharia had acknowledged that she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practising law in the United States.
She had earlier described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.

stories.title: Israeli president picks Netanyahu's rival Gadi Eisenkot to try to form government
summary: Israel’s president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s strongest rival, to try to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power.

At the end of the consultations, factions comprising 67 Knesset members recommended to the president that Yashar party’s Eisenkot be tasked with forming the government, while factions comprising 46 Knesset members recommended Likud’s Netanyahu, the statement noted.

His potential pathways to power include trying to form a minority government with Arab support from the outside; forming a coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties that he and his allies have shunned in the past; or forging a unity government with Netanyahu.

stories.title: Clashes erupt in Paris amid new protests across France
summary: Thousands of people protested across France on Saturday in a new show of anger against the government, with clashes erupting between police and some protesters in Paris despite a lower turnout than in previous weeks.
A total of 146,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Saturday, including 46,000 in Paris, the interior ministry said.
At the end of the protest in Paris, police used tear gas against individuals throwing projectiles and homemade fireworks at the security forces, an AFP correspondent said.

stories.title: CM Bugti's remarks about FWO's performance taken out of context: Balochistan minister
summary: GWADAR: Balochistan Planning Minister Mir Zahoor Ahmad Buledi has said Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti’s recent remarks regarding the Frontier Works Organisation (FWO) had been presented out of context.

Speaking on a point of order in the Balochistan Assembly in late October, Baloch, a former chief minister, had criticised the contracting process for road projects and alleged that the FWO had awarded work according to its own preferences.
Reiterating his position on the broader situation and development agenda in Balochistan, Buledi defended the FWO, terming its overall performance in the province commendable.

stories.title: Poland says 6 killed in shooting in central Krakow
summary: Poland’s police said on Saturday that six people were killed and around a dozen wounded after a gunman opened fire in the historic centre of its second city, Krakow.
A man drove a car onto Krakow’s Main Square and began shooting at random people, said police.
The gunman acted alone and is Polish, a police spokeswoman told AFP. “There is one perpetrator; it is a Polish man,” she said by phone.

stories.title: Pakistan's men down South Korea to win Asian Team Squash title
summary: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan defeated South Korea 2-0 in the men’s final of the 23rd Asian Team Squash Championship at the Mushaf Squash Complex on Saturday.
In the men’s final, Pakistan’s Noor Zaman and Asim Khan outclassed their respective opponents.
In the women’s final, Hong Kong China downed Malaysia 2-1 to become Asian champions.

stories.title: Govt announces auto policy with focus on cheaper vehicles, EVs
summary: The federal government on Saturday introduced the new auto policy, with a special focus on cheaper vehicles and electric vehicles (EVs).

He explained that the policy rested on six pillars: cheaper vehicles, especially for the middle class and lower middle class; encouraging exports; localisation; vehicle safety; promotion of EVs; and transparency.

The adviser said that the government intends to finance the proposed incentives for EVs through an automotive development levy (ADL) on vehicles powered by internal combustion engines (ICE) above 1,000cc — ordinary cars.

stories.title: Pakistani startup led by Nust graduate wins award at Silicon Valley summit
summary: Pakistani startup RLabs has won the best startup award at the Silicon Valley November Summit in California, with the government on Saturday hailing the achievement as showcasing the “growing strength of our startup ecosystem”.
RLabs, a Pakistani startup incubated at the National Incubation Centre for Aerospace Technologies (Nicat) and led by Harris Ahmed, won the ‘GOAL Startup Award’ at the summit.

She reaffirmed the government’s vision: “Pakistani startups should not just compete globally, but help shape the future of technology.” “Congratulations to Harris Ahmed and the entire RLabs team for making Pakistan proud.

stories.title: Pakistan Information Commission seeks disclosure of travel allowances, perks and expenses of NA committees
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Pakistan Information Commission (PIC) has directed the National Assembly Secretariat to provide detailed information regarding expenditures, travel allowances, perks and privileges of chairpersons and members of parliamentary standing committees and subcommittees.

In the order, available with Dawn, the PIC directed the secretary of the NA Secretariat to provide clear and specific responses to 13 outstanding questions under the Right of Access to Information Act 2017 (RTI Act) within 10 days.
Thus, the PIC directed the NA Secretary to provide complete and specific responses to questions numbered 2 to 14 within 10 days.

stories.title: When home is hell
summary: In May, a father in Vehari repeatedly raped his three daughters aged 14, 11, and nine for six consecutive months; while three children aged six, four, and three were killed and found hanging from the fans in their home in Multan.
Homes repeatedly turn into hell for children as our criminal justice system is unequipped to intercept and prevent attacks within the home.
Around 2,000 cases of child abuse were reported in just the first six months of the current year.

stories.title: Expanding on naval blockade, US military looks to restrict Iranian land commerce
summary: Building on a months-long naval blockade on Iran, the US military ‌said on Saturday it is launching a task force to help crack down on Tehran's movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material over its land borders and through the Caspian Sea.

Iran's secret network A Reuters investigation found Iran has created a ​secret network of military agencies to import at least $2 billion in hardware, explosives and heavy-duty trucks since January 2025, evading both ​the US naval blockade and Western sanctions.

Reuters has reported that US intelligence assessments in recent months have indicated that renewed strikes on Iran would not fundamentally ​change Tehran's negotiating position or lead to the fall of Iran's government.

stories.title: India says landed heavy-lift military aircraft at highest altitude
summary: The Indian Air Force said on Saturday it had successfully landed a heavy-lift transport aircraft at the highest altitude anywhere in the world in remote Ladakh bordering China.

The military airfield at Nyoma was completed last year as part of a push for military infrastructure in the icy region following a border clash in 2020 that killed 20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers.
However, deep distrust remains and both sides maintain military deployments along their roughly 3,500-kilometre high-altitude border along Tibet owing to unresolved territorial disputes.

stories.title: Trump accuses Democrats of threatening Republicans after midterm win
summary: US President Donald Trump on Saturday accused Democrats of threatening Republican officials, donors and supporters with impeachment and imprisonment following their midterm election victory, describing the alleged actions as “extortion at the highest level”.

The allegations come amid heightened political tensions following the midterm elections, with control of Congress and the balance of power in Washington expected to shape the next phase of Trump's presidency.
Trump did not provide specific details of the alleged threatening letters or identify the individuals he said had received them.

stories.title: Would a strike on Iran’s nuclear facilities impact Pakistan?
summary: Other nuclear facilities, including research reactors, fuel fabrication plants, uranium conversion facilities, and radioactive material storage locations, may also present some risk of radiological releases.

Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant and spent fuel storage: Potentially serious transboundary radiological consequences in the event of a severe accident, although such an outcome is not inevitable and would depend on the nature and extent of the damage.

It is scientifically inappropriate to assume that damage to Iranian uranium enrichment and nuclear fuel-cycle facilities would necessarily expose neighbouring countries to significant levels of radiation.

stories.title: China successfully launches CERES-2 carrier rocket
summary: The rocket blasted off at 7:37 a.m. (Beijing Time) from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China and successfully sent the satellites into a 535-km sun-synchronous orbit.
The four satellites belong to different fields, ranging from ocean remote sensing and commercial meteorology to university-led scientific research and space situational awareness.
The rocket development team said the successful flight test and the precise orbital insertion of the four satellites mark the official entry into service of a new commercial launch vehicle.

stories.title: Democrats secure additional US House seats as more midterm races called
summary: Democrat Aisha Wahab secured victory in California’s 14th Congressional District as more races were called following the US midterm elections, while 19 remained undecided as of Saturday.
Read: US midterms deliver wave of historic firsts across states, Congress Democrat Rep. Aisha Wahab wins reelection to the U.S. House in California's 14th district, CBS News projected.

Decision Desk HQ separately projected that Republican incumbent Mario Diaz-Balart had defeated Democrat Nicole Locklin in Florida’s 26th District, although the Associated Press had not called the race as of Saturday morning.

stories.title: Astronomers spot white dwarf star with two rings of planetary debris
summary: Researchers have now spotted ‌a white dwarf with planetary debris swirling around it in an unusual configuration that may offer a peek into one possible outcome for our solar system in the distant future.
Some surviving rocky bodies may have been gravitationally perturbed onto highly eccentric orbits that brought them close to the white dwarf," Lagos-Vilches said.

This ⁠suggests that they may originate from different parent bodies, or possibly from different layers of a rocky body that was disrupted when it went too close to the white dwarf due to its strong gravitational field," Lagos-Vilches said.

stories.title: Environmental groups embrace AI, even as they warn of data center impacts
summary: Environmental groups worldwide are using artificial intelligence to analyze climate data, track forest fires and count endangered wildlife – embracing a technology they also warn is driving a surge in electricity demand, water use and greenhouse-gas emissions.
Reuters interviewed 15 major environmental, conservation and development organizations about their AI use.

"While other organizations are asking how to use AI responsibly, Greenpeace is asking whether it's necessary to build all these ​massive data centers in the first place," said Katrin Xueying Wu, a climate and energy campaigner with the organization.

stories.title: Israel's president pledges to pick candidate on Sunday to form government
summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's main rival secured nods on Thursday from a majority of ‌lawmakers to try to form a government, but Israel's president said it was still unclear who could break the election deadlock as he pledged to nominate a candidate on Sunday.

Read: Israeli president receives official election results as committee rejects fraud allegations Herzog held marathon talks with elected factions ⁠on Wednesday and Thursday, during which 67 of parliament's 120 elected lawmakers endorsed Eisenkot, while 46 endorsed Netanyahu.

In a setback for the prime minister on Thursday, United Torah Judaism, one of two major parties representing ultra-Orthodox Jewish voters and a longstanding Netanyahu coalition ally, declined to recommend any candidate to form ​a government during talks with Herzog.

stories.title: Smog, hazardous air quality grips parts of Punjab amid dry weather forecast
summary: Wagha Border recorded an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 500, classified as hazardous, while Barki Road reported an ‘unhealthy’ reading of 288.
Meanwhile, Lahore's US AQI reading on IQAir's live monitoring platform stood at 275 on Saturday morning, improving to 172 by the evening, although air quality remained in the unhealthy category.

Although Lahore did not feature among the 10 cities in the latest provincial ranking, station-level readings indicated that several parts of the provincial capital continued to experience unhealthy air quality.

stories.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ set to dominate box office as ‘The Cat in the Hat’ targets second place
summary: Godzilla Minus Zero is heading towards a strong opening weekend at the North American box office, with the Japanese monster sequel expected to outperform new releases including Warner Bros.’ animated adaptation of The Cat in the Hat.
Directed by Takashi Yamazaki, Godzilla Minus Zero is projected to earn approximately $30 million from 3,254 theatres across the US and Canada during its opening weekend.
The sequel follows the success of 2023’s Godzilla Minus One, which earned $11.4 million during its North American opening weekend before eventually collecting approximately $57 million domestically.

stories.title: Supreme Court terms lawyers' vigilance 'foundational' to protecting clients' cases from dismissal
summary: ISLAMABAD: Emphasising the importance of diligent case presentation, the Supreme Court on Saturday reiterated that an advocate’s absolute vigilance was a “foundational requirement” for protecting a client’s case from dismissal in default.
On Saturday, Justice Mazhar emphasised that, if an advocate lacks a sense of his professional duty, the ultimate sufferer was the client who engaged the advocate on reposing confidence in him.

This was because the “indispensable purpose of a court is to determine the actual disputes as an elementary virtue of the administration of civil and criminal justice”. “The rules of procedure are meant to serve justice and not obstruct it,” the judgment concluded.

stories.title: Pakistani astronaut to join Shenzhou-24 mission to China's space station
summary: A Pakistani astronaut will travel to China’s Tiangong space station aboard the Shenzhou-24 mission, becoming the first foreigner to visit the orbiting outpost, Beijing’s manned space agency said on Saturday.
PM Shehbaz hoped that the space mission would “add new dimensions to the brotherly relationship between Pakistan and China”.
Under the pact, two Pakistanis were to train in China, with one joining a mission on the Tiangong space station operated by Beijing.

stories.title: Rubio warns top staff against conflicts of interest as Republicans look to 2028
summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has moved to tighten control over the State Department, telling senior ​officials that staff must stay in their lanes and avoid actions that present conflicts of interest, four people familiar with the matter said.

Soon after the meeting, three ​of the people said the State Department's policy chief, Jeremy Lewin, was forced out of his job in part due to concerns that he was working on matters outside his area without proper coordination.

Asked for comment, a State Department official said: "It ​was mutually agreed it was time [for Lewin] to move on." Lewin said in a statement to Reuters that his departure was planned several weeks before it was announced and he denied he was fired.

stories.title: PHC strikes off petitions against emergency, governor’s rule from cause list
summary: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Saturday removed all writ petitions challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), as well as arrests made under the Maintenance of Public Order (3-MPO) ordinances, from its cause list.
Several high-profile petitions challenging the emergency and governor’s rule were pending before the PHC.

The federal government had repeatedly warned that governor’s rule or an emergency could be imposed, accusing the provincial administration of failing to cooperate adequately with the Centre on counterterrorism.

stories.title: PCB adds Aamir Jamal, three uncapped players to Pakistan squad for Sri Lanka Tests
summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Saturday added pace-bowling all-rounder Aamir Jamal and three uncapped players to the Test squad for the two-match series against Sri Lanka, taking the strength of the team to 16.

Batter Mohammad Tayyab Arif, fast bowlers Ali Shabbir and Saqib Khan have earned their maiden call-ups following impressive performances in domestic cricket and the PCB Patron’s XI’s three-day practice match against Sri Lanka at the Islamabad Club from November 4 to 6.
Razaullah made an impressive impression on his Test debut against England at Edgbaston earlier this year, taking four wickets before scoring a rapid 81, which included nine sixes.

stories.title: ECP issues notice to Attaullah Tarar for alleged code of conduct violation ahead of NA-77 by-election
summary: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Saturday issued a notice to Information Minister Attaullah Tarar for allegedly violating the code of conduct during the by-election in NA-77 Gujranwala.

According to a press release issued by the office of the Punjab Provincial Election Commissioner, the district monitoring officer issued the notice after Tarar participated in the election campaign of Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) candidate Rashid Bashir Warraich.

Warraich has been accused of violating the code of conduct by inviting Tarar to the constituency to participate in his election campaign and has further been directed to appear before the district monitoring officer at 11am on November 8 and submit an explanation.

stories.title: After midterm rout, Vance tries to build his own 2028 brand
summary: Three people familiar with the White House and Vance's communications told Reuters that the vice president was not breaking with Trump and said White House chief of staff Susie Wiles knew in advance about Vance's post.

The dialogue further elevated Vance as a potential post-Trump conservative standard-bearer, said Michael Ricci, a Republican strategist and former adviser to House Speakers John Boehner and Paul Ryan.
White House representatives referred Reuters to Trump's comments on Wednesday, when he told reporters he understood ​Vance's perspective on the election results.

stories.title: PML-N's ex-AJK PM Raja Haider appeals to authorities to 'intervene before it's too late' in Rawalakot
summary: The city is currently gripped by unrest amid alleged clashes between security forces and supporters of the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) rights group, with casualties reported.
Tensions escalated after the AJK government proscribed the JAAC on June 6, ahead of a planned long march and protest on June 9.
In August, the PML-N formed a government in the region after securing a majority in the AJK elections, with Barrister Syed Iftikhar Ali Gilani elected as the prime minister.

stories.title: Russian diplomats and military officials to join talks with US and Ukraine, Kremlin says
summary: Russia's delegation to talks with the United States and Ukraine next week will include senior military officials and diplomats, including ​Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told ‌Interfax news agency.

Russia's delegation, headed again by Kremlin aide ​Vladimir Medinsky as chief negotiator, will include Ryabkov for the ⁠first time as well as Yuri Zhigarlovsky, a senior General Staff officer, the ​report said.
All members of the delegation met Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday at a Russian Security Council meeting that was partly devoted to the upcoming talks.

stories.title: LPG availability, fair pricing among govt priorities, says petroleum minister
summary: Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said on Saturday that addressing public concerns over the availability and unfair pricing of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) was a government priority.
According to state-run Radio Pakistan, the minister attended the first meeting of the committee formed to ensure transparent auction of LPG.
Earlier this week, Malik assured the public that the government will make utmost efforts to meet the demand for LPG during the winter months.

stories.title: Bushra Bibi approaches IHC over worsening eyesight, seeks treatment from doctors of her choice
summary: Meanwhile, Barrister Salman Safdar, counsel for the PTI founder, has submitted an affidavit before the IHC detailing his recent meeting with Imran and Bushra at Adiala jail and raising serious concerns about her eyesight.
Barrister Safdar stated that Bushra had specifically requested that her medical examination and treatment be conducted by her personal doctors.

The application urges the IHC to intervene to ensure that Bushra receives immediate specialist medical attention and that her deteriorating eyesight is not further compromised due to any delay in treatment.

stories.title: Win for students: LHC directs two private medical colleges to adjust, refund excess fees by Nov 29
summary: It held that the institutions must implement the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council’s (PM&DC) prescribed fee limits in accordance with the regulator’s notifications and the court’s findings.

The court noted that the petitioner institutions had submitted their audited financial statements and sought enhancement of the prescribed tuition fees through the Pakistan Association of Medical Institutions (PAMI).

The court also recorded the specific annual tuition fee ceilings prescribed for the two institutions under the March 11 notification: Rs2,026,341 for University Medical and Dental College, Faisalabad, and Rs2,052,099 for FMH College of Medicine and Dentistry, Lahore.

stories.title: Could Robert Pattinson become the next James Bond? The actor joins 007 casting race
summary: Robert Pattinson has reportedly screen tested for the role of James Bond, placing the Batman star among the contenders to take over the iconic 007 character.
Pattinson’s other recent and upcoming projects include Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and the A24 film The Drama.
Amazon declined to comment on the reported screen tests, and no official announcement has confirmed Pattinson as the next 007.

stories.title: Govt unveils new auto policy aimed at promoting EVs, boosting localisation
summary: The federal government on Saturday unveiled a new auto policy aimed at promoting electric vehicles (EVs) and boosting localisation, while aiming to reduce the country’s fuel import bill.
Tarar added: "The new auto policy aims to promote innovation, value addition and localisation in the domestic automobile industry to create employment opportunities and enable vehicle exports.

He added that the broader objective of the new auto policy was to reduce production costs, encourage investment in local manufacturing, create employment opportunities and make Pakistani vehicles more competitive in international markets.

stories.title: US Chargé d'Affaires, Balochistan officials mark completion of Mehrgarh Museum project
summary: The United States Chargé d’Affaires (CDA) Natalie Baker on Saturday joined Balochistan's Parliamentary Secretary Nawabzada Mir Muhammad Zarain Khan Magsi and the leadership of the Sindh Exploration and Adventure Society (SEAS) to "mark the successful completion of the US Ambassadors Fund for Cultural Preservation (AFCP) project for the Mehrgarh Museum of Balochistan," representing the first-ever AFCP initiative in Balochistan.

According to a press release, the project, implemented with the SEAS and the Balochistan Culture Department, "preserved ancient Neolithic and archaeological artefacts from the historic Mehrgarh civilisation, upgraded museum curation to international standards, expanded community outreach, and trained local heritage professionals to ensure long-term collection care." The release stated that the "AFCP footprint now spans all four provinces of Pakistan, reinforcing the US’ enduring commitment to protecting Pakistan’s rich cultural heritage." In her address at the completion ceremony, CDA Baker "highlighted the power of American expertise to deliver tangible, lasting results and foster trust between the peoples of both nations," the release said.

Read: US, SBP celebrate deployment of new core banking network and data centre CDA Baker stated that "through American excellence in museums and heritage preservation, the Mehrgarh Museum of Balochistan will showcase the 8,000-year-old Mehrgarh civilisation and many others." According to the press release, she also noted that projects such as this one, "show what American expertise delivers: lasting, tangible results that preserve history, create jobs, and strengthen local communities." The CDA noted that "together, the US and Pakistan are making real progress in protecting this remarkable legacy." CDA Baker, Parliamentary Secretary Magsi, and project leads including Dr Asma Ibrahim and Dr Kaleemullah Lashari "unveiled a commemorative plaque that will stand at the entrance of the Mehrgarh Museum in Quetta ahead of its official reopening later this month," the release said.

stories.title: Australia's Khawaja claims entire team knew about 'Sandpapergate'
summary: Usman Khawaja claimed on Saturday that the entire Australian team knew about the 2018 “Sandpapergate” scandal in Cape Town and said they also employed the tactic during the previous Test at Port Elizabeth.

Captain Steve Smith, his deputy David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were sent home in disgrace and found by a Cricket Australia investigation to be the only three players with prior knowledge of the ball-tampering plot.

You get to a place where you move on, and I’ve moved on with my life.” In the book, according to the newspaper, Khawaja recounts that discussions about ways to rough up the ball were first held in the dressing room during the second Test at Port Elizabeth, now known as Gqeberha.

stories.title: Pakistan, Sudan sign visa-free travel agreement for official, diplomatic passport holders
summary: Pakistan and Sudan on Saturday signed an agreement allowing holders of official and diplomatic passports to travel between the two countries without obtaining visas.
Pakistan and Italy also signed an agreement in June this year abolishing visa requirements for diplomatic passport holders, aimed at facilitating exchanges between the two countries.
In April 2025, Pakistan and Hungary signed an agreement abolishing visa requirements for diplomatic passport holders.

stories.title: Pakistan calls for strategic reform, not budget cuts, to shield UN peacekeeping
summary: Read: UN chief praises Pakistan's peace efforts on regional conflicts in meeting with CDF Munir While support for peacekeeping remained broad, “consistent political backing is harder to secure”, the UN official said.
With peacekeeping facing mounting political, operational and financial pressures, Ambassador Shah underscored that its relevance remained undiminished.
Peacekeeping, he said, remained a cost-effective and vital mechanism for maintaining international peace and security, adding that it should be built upon and strengthened rather than undermined.

stories.title: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war
summary: Iran said Saturday its military has grown “stronger” since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran’s nuclear programme.
Reward offered The US military said it was offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear programme.
Early on Saturday, Iran’s Tasnim news agency reported that two missiles had struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, adding there was no official information about any damage.
